page: Amazon Web Services c5a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz across 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, with hardware support for standard x86 extensions such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and SHA extensions, but without support for AVX-512 instruction sets.

The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes no bundled local instance storage, requiring all persistent root and secondary volumes to be attached as remote Elastic Block Store volumes. Network capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or dedicated GPUs are present.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier compute capabilities alongside measurable memory subsystems constraints. Multi-core performance sits reliably within median cloud tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7998.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 19648.81. However, single-core throughput is constrained, registering a stress-ng single-core score of 767.39. While cached small-block memory throughput reaches 800.68 GB/sec, uncached 256 MB block memory operations show reduced bandwidth, yielding 37.14 GB/sec on read and 22.42 GB/sec on write.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the AMD-based compute tier offers high vCPU density for multithreaded integer workloads, software compilation, batch processing, and distributed web serving where dedicated core access is prioritized over raw memory bandwidth or local disk I/O.
description: Amazon Web Services c5a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, 32.0 GB of DDR4 system memory at 3 GHz, and a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps. It contains no onboard local storage or dedicated graphics accelerators, necessitating remote block storage for operating system and data requirements. Benchmark profiles indicate solid multi-core computational throughput, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core rating of 7998.0 and PassMark CPU score of 19648.81, though uncached memory write and read bandwidth display comparatively lower throughput. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio establishes the instance as a cost-efficient platform for batch computing, CI/CD compilation, multi-threaded container workloads, and web serving architectures requiring high vCPU counts without high memory footprints.
